change_summary: Added an audit-only runner that replays the accepted A+B stack on the three fixed snapshots and records candidate-day cohort composition across generate/enrich/pre-size/entry stages to test whether same-day opportunity composition is a richer sleeve-selection state than the rejected cheap day-state proxies.
hypothesis: Candidate-day cohort composition may be a richer replayable sleeve-selection state than the rejected cheap day-state proxies.
notes: Observed-only alpha research. The accepted stack's decision surface is mostly sparse: most trading days have no candidates and most active days have only 1-2 pre-size candidates. Mixed or dominant multi-candidate cohort days are rare across all three fixed windows, which explains why broad day-state sleeve routers were unstable. The useful next step is not another OMDB/QQQ-SPY day-state sweep, but a tie-break or slot-collision mechanism targeted only at rare true cohort-competition days.
